assumptions: mass_value represents a physical amount and therefore must be nonnegative.
One tonne is normalized to 1000 kg; the raw value and raw unit remain immutable.
Blank feature is missing, while feature value 99 is a documented device-mode sentinel rather than an ordinary measurement.
No unlisted category equivalence is assumed: Red, R, red, BLUE, blue, and green remain distinct until a mapping is approved.
The intended deployment population and whether prediction targets future observations or unseen entities are unspecified.

baseline.description: Naive row-level random split with all exported columns available as predictors.
evidence: Repeated entities and the exact duplicate can contaminate row-level partitions.
target_copy reproduces target exactly, and future_score is post-outcome information; either can create spuriously perfect prediction.
No baseline performance metric was computed because executing this baseline would rely on known leakage.

candidate_models: Audit candidate A: regularized linear regression after train-only normalization, category encoding, explicit missing/sentinel indicators, and exclusion of row_id, entity, date, future_score, target_copy, and target from predictors. Fit and metrics were not run because the prediction objective and deployment regime are unspecified.

Audit candidate B: a shallow tree-based regressor using the same leakage exclusions and train-only preprocessing. It could model nonlinear mass effects but has greater overfit risk and implementation complexity on at most nine eligible rows. Fit and metrics were not run.

Split candidate A: deterministic entity-grouped outer evaluation, preferably leave-one-entity-out with six folds, plus training-only preprocessing. This is structurally appropriate for unseen-entity generalization but produces tiny one-entity test folds.

Split candidate B: entity-aware rolling-origin evaluation for future observations. The present data cannot support a clean joint test of future and unseen-entity generalization because D, E, and F occur only on 2026-01-01 and several entities have too few dates.
Rejected alternative: ordinary random or stratified row splitting, because it does not control duplicate or entity leakage.

data_findings: Confirmed duplicate: CSV data rows 5 and 6 are byte-equivalent after parsing; both have row_id 5. The identifier 5 occurs twice and identifier 6 is absent.
Confirmed missingness: feature is blank only for row_id 3; all other inspected fields have zero blank values.
Confirmed invalid physical value: row_id 4 has mass_value -5 kg and requires quarantine or source correction, not silent clipping.
Mixed units are present. Row_id 3 has 0.012 tonne, which normalizes to 12 kg and is plausible; this is not an error.
Row_id 9 has 250 kg. The dictionary permits values through 300 kg, so this is a plausible extreme and must not be removed solely by an outlier rule.

Row_id 8 has feature 99. The dictionary identifies 99 as a device-mode sentinel, so treating it as a continuous value would be erroneous; retain the raw value and encode a sentinel/missingness indicator under an approved rule.

Category labels are inconsistent or potentially aliased: red=4, Red=1, R=1, blue=1, BLUE=2, green=2. Case normalization can support red/Red and blue/BLUE, but R-to-red remains an unresolved semantic mapping.
Direct leakage is confirmed: target_copy equals target on all 11 rows, with Pearson correlation 1.0 and offset 0 throughout.
Temporal leakage is confirmed: future_score is documented as recorded one day after target and equals target+1 on all 11 rows, with Pearson correlation 1.0.
Entity repetition creates row-split leakage risk: entity counts are A=3, B=3, C=2, D=1, E=1, F=1 before quarantine/deduplication.
Input order is not chronological within entity A: dates occur as 2026-01-01, 2026-01-03, 2026-01-02. Temporal operations must sort explicitly by entity and date.
Only 10 unique rows and six entities remain after exact deduplication; quarantining the negative-mass row leaves nine analysis-eligible rows. Any performance estimate would be highly uncertain.
experiment_design: First preserve the raw files and register their hashes; create only derived views for corrections.
Deduplicate by full-row identity through a recorded exclusion flag, and quarantine the negative-mass record pending source resolution.
Exclude future_score and target_copy before any split or feature analysis.
Choose the deployment estimand at a human gate: unseen entities, future observations of known entities, or both.

For unseen-entity evaluation, use deterministic leave-one-entity-out outer folds; perform imputation, category handling, sentinel encoding, scaling, feature selection, and tuning solely within each outer training set.
Report fold-level predictions and errors rather than only an aggregate, because six entities and unequal row counts make aggregate metrics unstable.

If future-known-entity prediction is selected, require more longitudinal observations and use rolling-origin splits sorted by date with an appropriate temporal gap; do not reuse the current entity-holdout result as temporal evidence.
Compare any trained candidate with a training-fold-only constant/median baseline, but defer fitting until the target metric and deployment regime are approved.
falsification_tests: The direct-leakage finding would be falsified if an authoritative lineage record showed target_copy was available independently before target creation; the local dictionary instead states it is derived from target.

The temporal-leakage finding would be falsified only if deployment occurs after future_score becomes available and target prediction remains meaningful at that later time; current timing documentation says it is recorded one day after target.
The duplicate finding would be falsified if the two identical exports represented intentionally weighted independent events; no such weight or event identifier is present.
The negative-mass error classification would be falsified if mass_value were documented as a signed adjustment rather than an amount; the current dictionary calls it an amount.
The R category mapping must remain unresolved unless authoritative domain metadata confirms or rejects R as red.
The selected split design must be reopened if deployment concerns future observations of known entities rather than unseen entities.

constraints: Exclude target_copy and future_score from every predictor matrix.
Exclude target from predictors and use it only as the response.
Treat row_id as an identifier, not a predictor.
Quarantine the negative mass row pending correction and collapse or weight-control the exact duplicate through a recorded decision.
Do not infer category alias R without human confirmation.
Fit all learned transformations inside each training fold.
Do not claim a temporal-generalization estimate from the illustrative entity split.
notes: The illustrative split executed on raw rows produced train/validation/test counts 9/1/1 and zero entity intersections. It is a structural sanity check, not a recommended performance experiment.

The audit record should be append-only with finding_id, source file hash, row locator, field, raw value, proposed interpretation, severity, evidence, status, actor, timestamp, and supersedes_id. Corrections belong in derived data; raw files remain unchanged.
Any approved resolution appends a new decision or superseding event rather than overwriting the prior record.
formalization.objective: Produce a reproducible audit and minimize leakage and invalid-data contamination subject to preserving raw evidence; no predictive loss objective is selected without a deployment definition.
parameters: Mass conversion: kg multiplier 1; tonne multiplier 1000.
Ordering keys for any temporal operation: entity then parsed date.
Illustrative executable sanity assignment only: train entities A/B/C/D, validation E, test F.
units: mass_value occurs in kg and tonne; normalized analytical mass is kg.
date is calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form.
feature, future_score, target_copy, and target have no units specified in the local dictionary.
variables: Raw fields: row_id, entity, date, category, mass_value, mass_unit, feature, future_score, target_copy, target.
Candidate prediction-time variables after exclusions: category, normalized mass, feature value, feature-missing indicator, and feature-sentinel indicator.
Partition variable s(entity) assigns every entity wholly to one outer fold.
Audit status per finding: OPEN, QUARANTINED, APPROVED, REJECTED, or SUPERSEDED.

reality_constraints: Prediction-time features cannot include values recorded after the target time.
A field derived from target cannot be used as a predictor.
Rows belonging to one entity must not cross train, validation, and test partitions when evaluating unseen-entity generalization.
Exact duplicates must not be allowed to cross partitions or receive unintended extra weight.
Preprocessing, imputation, category mapping, and sentinel handling must be learned or fixed using training data and documentation only.
Bulk shipments up to 300 kg are explicitly possible, so 250 kg is not an error solely because it is extreme.

robustness_tests: Recompute audit results after sorting by entity/date to ensure findings do not depend on file order; only the order anomaly itself should change.
Compare results with the exact duplicate retained at controlled weight versus excluded; material changes would indicate duplicate sensitivity.
Report analyses with the 250 kg plausible extreme retained and in a sensitivity view excluded, without labeling it erroneous.
Represent feature sentinel 99 using both a dedicated mode category and a missing-plus-indicator scheme within training folds; compare fold-level stability.
Do not run sensitivity modeling until the invalid mass, category semantics, deployment estimand, and evaluation metric are resolved.
